title: 1999 AHSME Problem 12
statement: What is the maximum number of points of intersection of the graphs of two different fourth degree polynomial functions \(y = p(x)\) and \(y = q(x),\) each with leading coefficient \(1?\)

solutions.text:
The \(x\)-coordinates of the intersection points are the roots of \(p(x) - q(x).\) Because both leading coefficients are \(1,\) the \(x^4\) terms cancel, so \(p(x) - q(x)\) has degree at most \(3\) and therefore at most \(3\) roots. The bound is attainable, for example by taking \(p(x) = x^4\) and \(q(x) = x^4 - x(x-1)(x+1),\) whose graphs intersect at \(x = -1, 0, 1.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: The leading \(x^4\) terms cancel in \(p(x) - q(x)\)
